speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members may also access these materials through the MP@SGPARL app.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the course of my presentation, I will refer Members to the various annexes and then you can follow as I speak.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the past 10 years before COVID-19 hit, we had a fairly stable market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We grew HDB supply in step with demand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is because we saw household sizes falling as part of societal trends, with the nuclearisation of families and more singles wanting to live alone.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We opened up access to better meet housing aspirations of singles.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If you look at the chart, you will see that from 2001 to 2021, while the number of residents living in HDB flats increased by only 10%, we had increased the total number of HDB flats by 29% – almost a third.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, if you look at the boxes at the bottom of the chart, we have the 2011, 2016, 2021 BTO application rates, these were lower before COVID-19 and spiked up during the COVID-19 years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, these numbers have been skewed because of the higher application rates in the earlier years by singles.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If you take that away for 3-room and larger flats, the application rate in the non-mature estates was very low – one point something, two point something before COVID-19 hit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Home Price to Income ratio (HPI) – Members will be familiar with this concept – HPI measures broadly the number of years of total household income that it takes to pay for a home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2012, the HPI for a 4-room flat in a non-mature estate was six.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, about six years of total household income to afford a home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: From 2015 onwards, the HPI had dropped and remained below 5.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is because the annual increase of BTO flat prices in non-mature estates is less than 1%, lower than the 3% annual increase in incomes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members, please refer to Annex 3, the next page.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You can see that HDB resale prices also stayed fairly stable and even somewhat softer.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, from 2013 to 2019, the HDB Resale Price Index (RPI) experienced almost six consecutive years of decline, falling by around 12%.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But in the last three years, supply has become tight and resale prices have risen.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, our building programme took a very hard hit during COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Construction work was halted for a few months, there was a severe worker shortage, the supply of construction materials was disrupted and we had to shore up construction firms all over Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As you can see from Annex 4, in 2019, before COVID-19 hit, we completed some 12,000 flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2020 when COVID-19 hit, we completed fewer than 8,000 units.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When people saw that the supply of BTO flats was disrupted and project completions delayed, some decided to get a resale flat instead, so, demand for resale flats went up.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Others got worried and decided to join the BTO queue even earlier because they did not know if they could indeed successfully ballot for one on time and they also saw that the waiting times got lengthened because of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the demand for BTO flats also went up, causing further anxiety.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, there has been a marked shift in social norms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Young Singaporeans want to move out to live on their own earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This trend may have been accentuated by the pandemic, as many people worked from home and wanted more space of their own.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There was also a sharp rise in the resale prices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the ground, young couples shared with us their concern about the sharp rise in the resale prices, the perception that choice BTO projects in mature estates are more expensive and the overall worry that HDB flats may be out of reach.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We fully appreciate these anxieties, even as we work hard to ensure that BTO flat prices remain stable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We know that Singaporeans are unhappy about the longer wait times and the delays.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My HDB colleagues have been working hard to catch up on lost time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We completed more than 20,000 homes last year, 2022, the highest annual number in the past five years, reflecting a concerted effort by HDB and the contractors working together to catch up on lost time to help to complete delayed projects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we will press on to finish building another 20,000 flats this year, deliver more keys to waiting home buyers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have also ramped up the supply of BTO flats to meet the higher demand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2022, we launched over 23,000 new flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will launch another 23,000 new flats this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We had earlier introduced Shorter Waiting Time (SWT) flats before the pandemic, so you wait less than three years for a flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While there have been some delays, more than 8,000 of such flats will be completed in the next two years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have done more to prioritise First-Timer (FT) young couples.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We do so by setting BTO prices based on affordability outcomes rather than just pass on rising costs to buyers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, construction costs shot up almost 30% in this period.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we do not price BTO flats based on cost.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Instead, we look at the household income across different levels and establish what the prices of flats should be to make them affordable to flat buyers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In non-mature estates, BTO flats are typically priced at around a Mortgage Servicing Ratio (MSR) of 25% or less, to ensure that buyers can use less than a quarter of their household income to pay for the mortgage instalment with little to no cash outlay.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In mature estates where the locations are more diverse, MSR can exceed 25% in certain areas, with HPI of around five times or more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also establish the market value of our new flats, based on the recent transacted prices of comparable resale flats nearby.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As you can see, we have kept BTO prices relatively stable even as median household incomes have increased.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To launch BTO flats at selling prices that are below market and are affordable to flat buyers across different income levels, we have to apply a substantial market discount.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On top of this, we provide generous grants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai claims that the Government has somehow lost its way and public housing is way too unaffordable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, for first-timers who apply for BTO flats in non-mature estates, virtually everyone gets a chance to select a flat within three tries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, more than eight in 10 buyers who collected their keys to BTO flats or bought resale flats last year, 2022, can service their monthly mortgage fully from their CPF contributions with little to no cash outlay.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Do you know the proportion of BTO flats that would be affordable to this family?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Is it half of all BTO flats because it is median?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, after two rounds of cooling measures last year, we are seeing some moderation in the rate of increase in resale prices and we are keeping a close watch.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is set against the context that 90% of Singaporeans own their homes today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: More remarkably, around 85% of our low-income households own their homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Generally, our HPI ratios are four to five times.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means that it takes around four to five years of total household income to buy a home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If you look at Annex 9, it shows how we compare with other major cities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In Hong Kong, it is more than 20 times.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, while there are concerns over resale prices, public housing remains broadly accessible and affordable today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My colleagues and I have been engaging a broad spectrum of Singaporeans on public housing in the past few months.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One of the concerns is over access to flats in mature estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The pandemic has also exacerbated this, as the highest application rates to mature estates over the past six years have all been in the last three years of this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We hear the reasons and aspirations of young couples.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They want to stay near parents and living nearer to transport nodes can save time in terms of going to work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They tell us because buying a home is one of their single largest life decisions, they feel they cannot compromise on location.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If it is the single most important buy, it must not be a "second-best" that they have to live with for years to come.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But mature estates are already built up and available new land is limited.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Despite these constraints, we have been doing our best to launch more projects in the mature estates in the last few years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the irony is this – the more BTO flats we supply in mature estates, the more buyers join the queue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Because Singaporeans can see that the subsidy in a BTO flat is real and realisable and that it means that after the Minimum Occupation Period (MOP), they can sell the flat if they need to move and make capital gain.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is especially the case for flats in mature estates because they are highly sought after.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Would it then help to price these flats even lower?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If we did so, we would be increasing the windfall gain that successful buyers enjoy and even more may join the queue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The result would be higher demand, greater competition for BTO flats in mature estates and greater anxiety among flat buyers all around.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the end of the day, this will not help first-timer couples who are looking for a flat to build their families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will also be unfair to all the families who failed to secure a flat in a mature estate and so missed out on the large windfall gain.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are not just building more flats in the mature estates but also consciously moderating the prices there.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, we launched the Prime Location Public Housing (PLH) model where public housing in prime, central locations come with additional subsidies to ensure that they remain affordable and accessible to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The quid pro quo is that they come with additional conditions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, flats in desirable locations in the mature estates cannot be priced at the same level as other flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even Mr Leong acknowledges the need for "price differences between locations" in his Facebook post.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are considering how to prevent the locational premiums from pricing out all but the most well-off buyers while avoiding an excessive windfall gain to those who successfully book such a flat in the mature estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition, I would like to encourage first-timer couples not to put your family plans on hold and consider a BTO flat in a non-mature estate first.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On our part, I would also like to assure Singaporeans that we are doing our utmost to improve the accessibility and affordability of HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We know that policies cannot remain static as the aspirations and needs of our people change and our society evolves.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is the reason why we have been engaging thousands of Singaporeans as part of our Forward Singapore engagements over the past few months.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After that, over a period of time, we will recalibrate our building programme so that SWT flats form a larger proportion of our supply of new flats than today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In this way, we reduce waiting times and better support the home ownership as well as marriage and parenthood aspirations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of demand, we will continue to review how we can better allocate flat supply to meet the most urgent housing needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In our public engagements, there has been one consistent point of agreement – that first-timers should be prioritised, especially those who are getting married as well as those with young children and who are looking to buy their very first home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are therefore studying how we can provide even more support for such first-timer families looking to buy their first homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also looking at measures to reduce the high rejection rate for BTO applications to ensure that BTO flats are prioritised for those with genuine and urgent housing needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we will consider if more housing support can be given to first-timer couples or first-timers buying a resale flat to help them in their home ownership aspirations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will announce these new measures when ready.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But in improving our policies on housing, we must as a responsible Government always ensure that they remain sustainable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our position is that we must maintain housing accessibility and affordability while keeping in mind other needs that Singaporeans have and ensuring that what we do is not at the expense of future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In essence, land in Singapore is extremely limited and we allocate limited land and resources to support housing needs with a few key principles in mind.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, we are committed to home ownership because a home that we can call our own roots us to Singapore and provides the basic stability for our families and our children to grow up in.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, our HDB flats are kept affordable with significant subsidies and grants for first timers and as a home for life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our housing policies are strongly geared towards ensuring that HDB flats are meant for living in, not for speculation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, we want public housing to be inclusive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We tier our grants to support the lower-income more so that despite their circumstances, they can still buy a home to build their families and their children can have a good environment to grow up in.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those who are not ready for home ownership, we provide public rental housing at heavily subsidised rates and paired up with ComLink to provide holistic social support for our tenants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our policies, such as the Ethnic Integration Policy, also seek to promote social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have recently made provisions to keep HDB flats in very central and attractive locations within the reach of the average Singaporean through the Prime Location Public Housing model.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, we believe that individuals have a key role to play too.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each one of us has to do our part to save up and meet our own housing needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That was a major motivation for us to create and develop the CPF system and I have explained how, with the CPF, public housing today is more affordable to most Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is easy to ask, why not make flats even cheaper?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a society, we have to debate and agree on how affordability should be fairly defined because ultimately, we, the people of Singapore, are all collectively paying for it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We already allocate substantive fiscal resources to support the Home Ownership Programme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many of us may not appreciate what this means.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To put this into perspective, the revenue from the 1% GST increase this year is less than half of this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What about the needs of our citizens for healthcare, education, transport and so on?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have heard many alternative proposals, including from Opposition Members of Parliament, and we give them the benefit of the doubt that the intent is to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But they are not as frank about the trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, Mr Leong Mun Wai says that BTO flats can be even cheaper if HDB does not have to pay for state land at fair market value.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have already explained that HDB does not price based on cost recovery.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: BTO flat pricing and BTO development costs are two separate and independent things.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, what Mr Leong has repeatedly asserted is plain incorrect.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We invest the reserves and use part of the investment returns to fund the Government's annual Budget and support the needs of current and future Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If HDB does not pay for fair market value for state land, it means that we are reducing the value of reserves and allocating more of it to today's housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By doing so, we are reducing the resources available to meet the other needs of today's generation as well as the needs of future generations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Leong deliberately avoids these trade-offs and sugarcoats the tough realities that we all face.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the Government cannot and will not take such an irresponsible approach.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Embedded in this commitment is also our vision for a strong and cohesive nation and an inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But what this Government believes equally in is to be frank about our challenges and trade-offs and explain how we seek to meet the competing needs of Singaporeans in the current generation as well as balance the needs of this generation with the needs of future generations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: (In Mandarin):   The Government understands that Singaporeans are concerned about public housing because of three key reasons: (a) high resale prices over the past three years; (b) the apparently high BTO flat prices in mature estates; and (c) the uncertainty in getting a chance to book a flat and the long waiting times for BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government is working hard to ensure that public housing remains affordable and accessible.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These flats will have waiting times of under three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After that, we will also recalibrate our building programme so that SWT flats will form a larger proportion of our supply of new flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of demand, we will continue to review how we can better allocate flat supply to first-timers, especially those who are getting married as well as those who have young children, and who are looking to buy their very first home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also looking at measures to reduce the rejection rate for BTO applications to ensure that BTO flats are prioritised for those with genuine and urgent housing needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will consider if more housing support can be given to first-timers buying a resale flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will announce these new measures when ready.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are not just building more flats in the mature estates but also consciously moderating the prices there.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, we launched the Prime Location Public Housing (PLH) model where public housing in prime and central locations will come with additional subsidies to ensure that they remain affordable and accessible for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also considering how to prevent locational premiums from pricing out all but the most well-off buyers, while avoiding an excessive windfall gain for those who successfully book such a flat in the mature estates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government has been committed to home ownership for our citizens since day one of our nation building.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As a responsible Government, we will always ensure that housing policies remain sustainable as we continue to improve them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our predecessors have worked hard to build the public housing system for Singaporeans so that we and our next generations will be able to have a better life than them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are the beneficiaries of their foresight and prudence and should do the same for the next generations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As we listen to different feedback and proposals, we should be frank about our challenges and the trade-offs and explain how we seek to meet the competing needs of Singaporeans in the current generation as well as future generations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government has always been frank and upfront about all these matters.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, our public housing is not perfect, but it has made housing accessible and affordable for Singaporeans and we must always keep improving it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ninety percent home ownership in a cosmopolitan city is not something that many other major cities have been able to achieve.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But these achievements are not just our own.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our predecessors worked so hard to build public housing for Singaporeans, worked so hard to pay for their own homes and above all, worked so hard to build up our reserves so that the next generations, including our own, would have a better life than them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we, the beneficiaries of their foresight and prudence, should inherit these same values and do the same for the next generation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In accordance with the decision of this House to take this Motion together with the next Motion standing in the name of Mr Leong Mun Wai, I will now call Mr Leong Mun Wai to move his Motion and make his opening speech before allowing Members to debate on both Motions.
